bugs.summary: perl = TRUE regex compile errors leak the PCRE character tables
bugs.creator: kevinushey

comments.text:
Every perl = TRUE regular expression that fails to compile leaks the PCRE character tables (1088 bytes with PCRE2) when the pattern is compiled in non-UTF-8 mode, i.e. with useBytes = TRUE or in a non-UTF-8 locale with unmarked input. strsplit(), grep(), gsub(), regexpr() and regexec() are all affected.

Analysis (trunk r90728):

R_pcre2_prepare() in src/main/grep.c builds the locale tables with pcre2_maketables() into a variable owned by its caller before calling pcre2_compile(); the callers free the tables only after their loop over the input vector. When compilation fails, the helper frees the compile context and then signals "invalid regular expression", and that error unwinds past the callers' cleanup, so the tables are never freed. R_pcre_prepare() (PCRE1) has the same shape around pcre_maketables().

The leak was found by OSS-Fuzz (testcase 6104737142079488, LeakSanitizer, through strsplit("", "\\", perl = TRUE, useBytes = TRUE)). On macOS, `leaks --atExit` over 300 iterations each of strsplit(), grepl() and gsub() with an invalid pattern and perl = TRUE, useBytes = TRUE reports 900 leaks (1152000 bytes) on trunk and none with the patch.

Proposed patch: attached as pcre-tables-leak.diff. Both helpers free the tables and reset the caller's pointer before signalling the compile error; nothing else refers to the tables at that point. make check passes.

The patch is also submitted as https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/388, where CI results and a reproducer can be seen.
